messages.subject: gl2fasta per chromosome?
messages.body_plain:
Happy New Year,

I often run gl2fasta to generate a concatenated alignment for phylogenetic analysis. Due to suspected gene flow among clades, I get low support at a few nodes on the tree. I see that the gl object includes columns "Chrom_*genus*", and that multiple sequence tags are located on a given chromosome/scaffold. Is there an easy way to concatenate sequence tags that share a chromosome, thus generating a separate fasta file for each? This format would allow us to conduct species tree analyses that might help explain the lack of support at given tree nodes.

Thank you,
Mike Sandel

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike

You can filter by chromosome and then export

Untested something like

For one level /chromisome you can use

Index <- gl@other$lic.metrics$chrom*genus*==“1”

gl2 <- gl.keep.loc(gl, loc.list=locNames(gl)[index])

and then gl2fasta on gl2

“1” is a place holder for your chromosome name

Also I would use a for loop or sapply in case you want to output more files

How pe that help.  This code is untested so there might be a typo in there but the general idea filter loci by chromosome and then output should work.

Cheers Bernd

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] AMOVA analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

To perform AMOVA using source and statut, you could use the below code:

library(dartRverse)
library(poppr)
gl <- your_genlight
# Converting genlight to genind
geni <- gl2gi(gl)
# Assign pop information to strata
strata(geni) <- data.frame(pop = pop(gl))
# Performing AMOVA
amova_po <- poppr.amova(geni,~pop,nperm = 100)
##AMOVA for statut
strata(geni) <- data.frame(pop = gl@other$ind.metrics$statut)
amova_Statut <- poppr.amova(geni,~pop,nperm = 100)
##AMOVA for origin
strata(geni) <- data.frame(pop = gl@other$ind.metrics$source)
amova_origin <- poppr.amova(geni,~origin,nperm = 100)

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: rdepth females and males
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christian,

Currently, there isn’t a straightforward way to obtain read depth by locus for each individual directly within dartR. However, you can request DArT to provide you with the counts file, which contains this information. Please note that dartR does not yet include any functions to extract or analyze this data directly.

If your goal is to identify sex-linked loci, I recommend exploring our dedicated package, dartR.sexlinked. Below are links to the GitHub repository and the relevant publication that provides more details on its usage and methodology:
dartR.sexlinked GitHub Repository <https://github.com/green-striped-gecko/dartR.sexlinked>
Relevant Article <https://doi.org/10.1111/1755-0998.13844>

I hope this helps! Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.body_plain:
Hi Juan,

Thank you for reporting that bug. The fix is available in the developing version of dartR.base. Please install this version as shown below:

# install developing version of dartR.base

# NOTE that in the below line you have to replace "_at_" by "@"

devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR.base_at_dev")

# OR

dartRverse::dartRverse_install(

  package = "dartR.base",

  rep = "Github",

  branch = "dev",

  verbose = TRUE

)

library(dartRverse)

x <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>

test_platypus_ss <- gl.subsample.loc(x,

                                     n = nLoc(x),

                                     replace = TRUE,

                                     error.check = TRUE)

test_platypus_ss <- gl.compliance.check(test_platypus_ss, verbose = 5)

Cheers,

Luis

messages.subject: Error with gl.LDNe (but actually gl2genepop)
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I've installed Ne Estimator on my Mac, and confirmed that it works with the included test dataset.

However, when I run gl.LDNe, I get this error:

Population     1 [Blackdown_364818_OMG_BRFDArT_]
Nondigit at locus 1, sample 2: [Blackdown_364820_OMG_BRFDArT_]
No population is run!
Error in str_split(res[res %like% "Lowest"], "\\s{3,}")[[1]] :
  subscript out of bounds

I tested this by running gl2genepop and trying to run it through Ne Estimator directly, it can read the right number of SNPs and the right number of populations, but says it's not in the right format, and again errors on the same individual.

Attached is the first pop section as output by gl2genpop (have 4 populations in reality). Any ideas on what is going wrong here with the format out of gl2genepop? I've checked that I don't have duplicate locus names.

Thanks,

Renee

messages.subject: Re: Error with gl.LDNe (but actually gl2genepop)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Renee,

It seems that there is a maximum number of characters for individuals labels in the program NeEstimator, but I couldn't find any specifics about this.
One solution is to change the individual names as below.

library(dartRverse)
load("glunlinkedSNPs.Rdata")
# reducing individuals names to 10 characters and make them unique
indNames(gl.unlinked.snps) <- make.unique(substr(indNames(gl.unlinked.snps),1,10),sep = "_")
r1 <- gl.LDNe(gl.unlinked.snps)

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: Differing measures of Heterozygosity
messages.body_plain:
Hello Sean,

I was wondering if you gained any insights about the differences observed for He/Hs across dartR and hierfstat. My situation is almost identical to yours, with the exception that FIS estimates also differ very slightly comparing the two packages (from 0.001 - 0.008).

Thanks,
David

On Friday, May 27, 2022 at 6:15:19 PM UTC-5 sea...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thanks for the response.
>
> Unfortunately with low coverage whole genome sequencing I do not have  samples or loci have no mussing data. I will keep both results and talk with some other population geneticist as I progress with my research.  The results from dartR are more of what I expected to see, in my populations so if  gl.report.heterozygosity somehow handles missing data differently I can see why He estimates would be lower than in Hierfstat.
>
> Thanks,
> Sean
> On Thursday, May 26, 2022 at 11:53:34 PM UTC-6 luis.m...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I think the differences come from how missing data and sample size are treated.
> >
> > In the latest version of dartR, the function gl.report.heterozygosity() was updated to include correction for sample size, including missing data (i.e. unbiased heterozygosity)
> > So the statistics you should look at from the output of the function is "uHe".
> >
> > To install the latest version of dartR:
> >
> > > devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR")
> >
> > You could also try removing all the missing data and testing all the functions again to see if you get the same results, for example:
> >
> > test <- gl.filter.callrate(your_gl, threshold = 1)
> >
> > Cheers,
> > Luis
> > On Friday, 27 May 2022 at 5:10:23 am UTC+10 sea...@gmail.com wrote:
> > >
> > > Hello,
> > >
> > > I am calculating diversity measures from a VCF table with over 60K SNPS. This data came from WGS methods and does have a large amount of missing data compared to RADseq.
> > >

The calculations for FIS and Ho are the same, but “He” is lower for each sample. Do you know why this would be and if the methods differ at all in their estimation of He?  I can see if missing data is handled differently between the two calculations it could explain the differences.
